q2_gaps: A characterizing generic whose subject is a SINGULAR INDEFINITE with a co-varying anaphor ("A Keeper's family keeps THAT Keeper's inherited station"). The Existential section rules that 'a/an' with a verbal predicate is a witness and reserves the generic/rule form for bare plurals and explicit quantifiers, and Donkey anaphora only maps a bound pronoun to a rule variable under an explicit quantifier - so a world rule stated in this form has no licensed universal encoding and can only be recorded as a one-off existential.
notes: Every local decision is doctrine-correct (Possession for both genitives possessed-first, participial 'inherited' kept as an adjective on the witness, keep -> Theme, singular collective 'family' with no GroupOf and no distribution, habitual so no tense). The consequence of the gap is that the sentence's generalization over Keepers is recorded as a single existential situation.
